framework.name: Cyber Essentials
framework.description: UK NCSC Cyber Essentials certification scheme - 5 technical controls to protect against common cyber attacks

controls.title: Firewall Protection
controls.description: Every device in scope must be protected with a correctly configured firewall (or network device with firewall functionality).

controls.title: Change Default Passwords
controls.description: Change default administrative passwords to a strong and unique password, or disable remote administrative access entirely.

controls.title: Restrict Admin Interface Access
controls.description: Prevent access to the administrative interface from the internet, unless protected by MFA or IP allow list with properly managed password authentication.

controls.title: Block Unauthenticated Inbound
controls.description: Block unauthenticated inbound connections by default.

controls.title: Document Firewall Rules
controls.description: Ensure inbound firewall rules are approved and documented by an authorised person, including the business need in the documentation.

controls.title: Remove Unnecessary Rules
controls.description: Remove or disable unnecessary firewall rules when they are no longer needed.

controls.title: Software Firewall on Untrusted Networks
controls.description: Use a software firewall on devices which are used on untrusted networks, such as public wifi hotspots.

controls.title: Remove Unnecessary User Accounts
controls.description: Remove and disable unnecessary user accounts (such as guest accounts and administrative accounts that won't be used).

controls.title: Change Default Passwords
controls.description: Change any default or guessable account passwords.

controls.title: Remove Unnecessary Software
controls.description: Remove or disable unnecessary software (including applications, system utilities and network services).

controls.title: Disable Auto-Run
controls.description: Disable any auto-run feature which allows file execution without user authorisation.

controls.title: Authenticate Users
controls.description: Ensure users are authenticated before allowing them access to organisational data or services.

controls.title: Device Locking Controls
controls.description: Ensure appropriate device locking controls for users that are physically present. Protect against brute-force attacks with throttling (max 10 guesses in 5 minutes) or locking after 10 unsuccessful attempts.

controls.title: Licensed and Supported Software
controls.description: All software on in-scope devices must be licensed and supported.

controls.title: Remove Unsupported Software
controls.description: Remove software from devices when it becomes unsupported, or remove from scope by using a defined sub-set that prevents all traffic to/from the internet.

controls.title: Enable Automatic Updates
controls.description: Have automatic updates enabled where possible.

controls.title: Apply Critical Updates Within 14 Days
controls.description: Apply updates within 14 days of release when they fix 'critical' or 'high risk' vulnerabilities (CVSS v3 base score of 7 or above), or when vulnerability severity is not specified by the vendor.

controls.title: User Account Creation Process
controls.description: Have in place a process to create and approve user accounts.

controls.title: Unique User Credentials
controls.description: Authenticate users with unique credentials before granting access to applications or devices.

controls.title: Remove Inactive Accounts
controls.description: Remove or disable user accounts when they're no longer required (e.g., when a user leaves the organisation or after a defined period of account inactivity).

controls.title: Implement MFA
controls.description: Implement multi-factor authentication where available. Authentication to cloud services must always use MFA.

controls.title: Separate Admin Accounts
controls.description: Use separate accounts to perform administrative activities only (no emailing, web browsing or other standard user activities that may expose administrative privileges to avoidable risks).

controls.title: Remove Special Access When Not Required
controls.description: Remove or disable special access privileges when no longer required (e.g., when a member of staff changes role).

controls.title: Password Brute-Force Protection
controls.description: Protect passwords against brute-force guessing using MFA, throttling (max 10 guesses in 5 minutes), or locking after 10 unsuccessful attempts.

controls.title: Password Quality Requirements
controls.description: Use technical controls to manage password quality: MFA, OR minimum 12 characters with no max limit, OR minimum 8 characters with deny list for common passwords.

controls.title: Password Management Support
controls.description: Support users to choose unique passwords: avoid common passwords, encourage longer passwords (minimum 3 words), provide secure password storage, do not enforce regular expiry or complexity requirements.

controls.title: Compromised Password Process
controls.description: Have an established process in place to change passwords promptly if you know or suspect a password or account has been compromised.

controls.title: Malware Protection Mechanism
controls.description: A malware protection mechanism must be active on all devices in scope. Use at least one of: anti-malware software or application allow listing.

controls.title: Anti-Malware Software Configuration
controls.description: If using anti-malware software, configure it to: be updated per vendor recommendations, prevent malware from running, prevent execution of malicious code, and prevent connections to malicious websites.

controls.title: Application Allow Listing
controls.description: If using application allow listing: only approved applications (restricted by code signing) are allowed to execute, actively approve applications before deploying, maintain a current list, users must not be able to install unsigned or invalid signature applications.
